name: "Hellkid" Johnny Lords
caption: The reigning Ironman Champion and leader of the stable Twisted Chaos, renamed Heaven's Gate in his honor after it won the promotion's own Stable Wars battle royal.

tenures.source: Billed throughout as the reigning Ironman Champion, retaining the title twice; led the renaming of his own stable to Heaven's Gate after its Stable Wars victory.
The EWWF's own Kingdom of the Wicked pay-per-view broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/kingdom-of-the-wicked-2002-08-21.html).
tenures.note: Shown watching from ringside and referenced by Adam Mitchell backstage as a figure wanting back into the company; the fed's own earlier incarnation is described as having gone bankrupt.

tenures.source: The EWWF's own 2 October 2002 Surrender broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/surrender-2002-10-02.html). The EWWF's own 10 October 2002 Surrender broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/surrender-2002-10-10.html).
tenures.note: Won two SEWF tournament rounds (over Vinnie Cepacelli, then Rocky Camarelli), each time with a hand on the tights; attacked repeatedly backstage by Harvester of Sorrow, Axel Reed and “Devilman” Christian Alicea.

tenures.source: The EWWF's own 5 December 2002 Surrender broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/surrender-2002-12-05.html).
tenures.note: Ambushed Axel Reed and “Devilman” Christian Alicea backstage before the show, then interfered repeatedly in the EWWF Championship three-way.

identity.note: A same-named RSPWF Top 200 stub carrying no federation tag at all; nothing ties it to this run.

name: Harvester of Sorrow
caption: A hardcore brawler who won the Extreme Championship from his own longtime rival in a two-out-of-three-falls scaffold match, then won the promotion's Stable Wars battle royal outright the same night.

tenures.source: Won the Extreme Championship from Farley Lane in a scaffold and steel cage match, then won the ten-man Stable Wars battle royal as the last man standing.
The EWWF's own 2 October 2002 Surrender broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/surrender-2002-10-02.html).
tenures.note: Debuted as one of Adam Mitchell's two hired enforcers, alongside Axel Reed, attacking Higor Rosa.

tenures.source: The SEWF's own 2001 broadcasts, 22 April 2001 to 29 April 2001.
tenures.note: The fed's own title histories place this name on its roster from 24 March 2001.

tenures.source: The EWWF's own 10 October 2002 Surrender broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/surrender-2002-10-10.html).
tenures.note: Beat Higor Rosa in a Last Man Standing match with help from Axel Reed and “Devilman” Christian Alicea, revealed as Ashlyn Summers' own kidnapper.

tenures.source: The EWWF's own 5 December 2002 Surrender broadcast (/promotions/ewwf-surrender-2002/archive/surrender-2002-12-05.html).
tenures.note: Assaulted Ashlyn Summers before the show while already billed the Extreme/Sex Champion, then won the EWWF Championship from Despair and Summers in a three-way.

name: Farley Lane
caption: A founding member of the stable calling itself the Old Breed, who lost the Extreme Championship to Harvester of Sorrow in a two-out-of-three-falls scaffold match after nearly matching him fall for fall.

tenures.source: Billed as the reigning Extreme Champion entering Stable Wars, lost the title there to Harvester of Sorrow and was eliminated from the Stable Wars battle royal soon after.

name: "Ironman" Mark Spencer
caption: A member of the Old Breed who came within a rung of taking the United States Championship in a ladder match before a returning ally's brass-knuckled interference cost him the win, then lost a grudge-match rematch to Luni.

tenures.source: Challenged Kenneth Morlock for the United States Championship in a ladder match (no title change); eliminated from the Stable Wars battle royal by a rival stable's interference; lost a grudge-match return to Luni.

name: "Crippler" Chris Rollins
caption: One half of the Family of Thugz, who helped retain the World Tag Team Championship twice alongside his partner Scorpio.

tenures.source: Retained the World Tag Team Championship with Scorpio against Farley Lane and Higor Rosa, then again against the Great Southern Rapist and Immortal Doomsday.

name: Scorpio
caption: The other half of the Family of Thugz, who helped retain the World Tag Team Championship twice before becoming the runner-up of the promotion's own Stable Wars battle royal.

tenures.source: Retained the World Tag Team Championship twice with Chris Rollins; reached the final two of the Stable Wars battle royal before being eliminated last by a returning Harvester of Sorrow.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (scorpio-mwa-millenium); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.
Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (scorpio-uwf-mar96); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Todd Zuckerwise
caption: The Family of Thugz's own manager, who stepped into the ring himself to beat Immortal Doomsday in a receipt-settling grudge match.

tenures.source: Managed the Family of Thugz through two successful tag title defenses; wrestled and beat Immortal Doomsday in a singles grudge match, with Chris Rollins running in to help finish it.

name: FBK
caption: The promotion's own on-screen Commissioner and leader of the Fourth Reich, who eliminated his own tag partner from the Stable Wars battle royal and later stole the disputed World Heavyweight Championship belt from its self-proclaimed holder's own locker room.

tenures.source: Served as the promotion's own Commissioner; teamed with and then turned on Simon Solkoff to eliminate both of them from the Stable Wars battle royal; ended the held record holding the disputed World Heavyweight Championship belt.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (full-blooded-killah-rspwf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.
Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (full-blood-killah-gswp-1999); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "The Shooter" Simon Solkoff
caption: A three-time former World Heavyweight Champion and member of the Fourth Reich who fell short in a Taipei Fist submission match, a World Title triangle match and a Lumberjack match across three cards.

tenures.source: Billed as a three-time former World Heavyweight Champion; lost an Ironman Championship submission match to Johnny Lords, was eliminated with FBK from the Stable Wars battle royal, then lost a Lumberjack match to Phantom.

identity.note: Shares a bare ring name with the held RSPWF Top 200 stub simon-solkoff-rspwf (tagged SEWF, 2001); no federation tag, date, or roster axis connects the two.

name: X-treme
caption: A chaotic, drug-addled member of the Fourth Reich who defected to Heaven's Gate between the promotion's own Stable Wars battle royal and its next broadcast.

tenures.source: Fought alongside Kenneth Morlock for the Fourth Reich in a World Title triangle match on 9 February; billed as a member of Heaven's Gate by the promotion's next broadcast, 15 February.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (x-treme-dpw-1996); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.
Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (x-treme-gmwe); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Outsider
caption: A returning member of the Fourth Reich, back from knee surgery, who challenged the roster to a rematch at the promotion's own upcoming anniversary card.

tenures.source: Returned from a torn tendon to issue an open challenge for the promotion's own upcoming anniversary card; helped attack Harvester of Sorrow and Hellkid Johnny Lords, and had his own arm broken by Harvester of Sorrow in the retaliation.

name: Guru
caption: The self-styled "Human Dictionary" and reigning World Heavyweight Champion, whose title defense was thrown into chaos when a rival stable stole the belt outright before a decision could be reached.

tenures.source: Billed as the reigning World Heavyweight Champion defending in a triangle match against Kenneth Morlock and X-treme when the Lynch Mob stole the belt from ringside before any fall.
The SEWF's own 2001 broadcasts, 29 April 2001.

identity.note: Shares a common ring name with three held wrestlers of unrelated federations and eras (guru-iewc-1998, guru-xpw-1999, guru-two-sewf); no operator, host, or roster axis connects any of them to this promotion.
Name-only collisions; nothing ties them to this run.

name: Preacher
caption: A rising member of Tony T's Masters of Wrestling who won the Internet Championship from Luni, defended it once, then lost it to the Great Southern Rapist by a surprise rollup.

tenures.source: Won the Internet Championship from Luni on 24 January; retained against Higor Rosa on 9 February; lost the title to the Great Southern Rapist on 15 February; defected from the Masters of Wrestling to Twisted Chaos in between.

identity.note: Shares a common ring name with several held wrestlers of unrelated federations and eras; no operator, host, or roster axis connects any of them to this promotion.

name: Phantom
caption: A 7'2" hardcore powerhouse who defected from Tony T's Masters of Wrestling to Heaven's Gate and won a Lumberjack match over Simon Solkoff with a shooting star press he calls the Phantom's Shadow.

tenures.source: Debuted alongside Preacher for the Masters of Wrestling, then defected with him to Twisted Chaos before Stable Wars; beat Simon Solkoff in a Lumberjack match on 15 February with a shooting star press.

identity.note: Shares a common ring name with numerous held wrestlers of unrelated federations and eras; no operator, host, or roster axis connects any of them to this promotion.

name: Tony T
caption: The promotion's own Vice President and manager of the Masters of Wrestling, whose priest-themed angle against Higor Rosa ended with both of his own charges torching the ring.

tenures.source: Managed the Masters of Wrestling (Preacher and Phantom) through a fire-and-religion-themed angle against Higor Rosa; both charges defected from his stable before the promotion's next broadcast.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (tony-t-kawf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: "Misfit" Chris Douvalas
caption: The leader of the Lynch Mob, who stole the World Heavyweight Championship belt outright and billed himself its self-proclaimed holder until the belt was stolen from him in turn.

tenures.source: Debuted against a returning Maxx Carnage on 9 February; had the Lynch Mob steal the disputed World Heavyweight Championship belt the same night; billed as the "self-proclaimed" champion on 15 February before FBK stole the belt from his own locker room.

identity.note: Shares a common ring nickname with the held character misfit (uwf, 2001-07), a different federation beginning two years after this record ends, with no operator or roster overlap.

name: Johnny Rotten
caption: A returning cruiserweight, blackballed a year earlier from a rival promotion, recruited into the Lynch Mob to replace Luni as its second member.

tenures.source: Debuted alongside Misfit Chris Douvalas in an ambush of Luni, billed as a former member of a since-collapsed promotion returning after a year away.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (johnny-rotten-napw); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Iam With Eyeconn
caption: The manager attached to both the Lynch Mob and the Mighty Mighty Posers, twice caught stealing the disputed World Heavyweight Championship belt for his own charges.

tenures.source: Managed Chris Douvalas and the Mighty Mighty Posers; stole the World Heavyweight Championship belt from ringside during the title's own triangle match before Luni took it from him.

name: Great Southern Rapist
caption: A member of the Janitors Crew who won the Internet Championship from Preacher with a surprise rollup after a bloody chair-and-table brawl.

tenures.source: Lost an Ironman Championship match to Johnny Lords on 24 January; teamed with Immortal Doomsday against the Family of Thugz on 9 February; won the Internet Championship from Preacher on 15 February.

name: Immortal Doomsday
caption: The Janitors Crew's own "Ice Cream Man," who lost a receipt-settling grudge match against the Family of Thugz's own manager, Todd Zuckerwise.

tenures.source: Teamed with the Great Southern Rapist against the Family of Thugz for the World Tag Team Championship on 9 February; lost a singles match to Todd Zuckerwise on 15 February.

name: Luni
caption: "The Lunatic" Ace Custis, a former Internet Champion who lost the title in a torch-and-barbed-wire gimmick match, then won a grudge-match return against Mark Spencer after switching from the Lynch Mob to Heaven's Gate.

tenures.source: Billed as the reigning Internet Champion, lost the title to Preacher on 24 January in a bat-above-the-ring gimmick match; grabbed the disputed World Heavyweight Championship belt amid the Stable Wars chaos before it was stolen from him; recruited into Heaven's Gate and beat Mark Spencer in a grudge-match return on 15 February.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named entity in another wing (luni-sewf); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in this wing's documents.

name: Malice
caption: One half of the tag team War Ensemble, later absorbed into Heaven's Gate after helping win the promotion's own Stable Wars battle royal for the stable.

tenures.source: Won a tornado tag match with Wasteland Warrior as War Ensemble on 9 February; billed as part of Heaven's Gate by the promotion's next broadcast.

name: Wasteland Warrior
caption: The other half of War Ensemble, absorbed into Heaven's Gate alongside his tag partner Malice.

tenures.source: Won a tornado tag match with Malice as War Ensemble on 9 February; billed as part of Heaven's Gate by the promotion's next broadcast.

name: Maxx Carnage
caption: A returning veteran wrestler who lost his comeback match to a debuting Chris Douvalas after a long absence from the ring.

tenures.source: Returned from a long absence to face a debuting "Misfit" Chris Douvalas on 9 February, losing after a top-rope finisher.

name: Enigma
caption: A mysterious, previously vanished wrestler who reappeared unmasked at the close of the promotion's own Stable Wars battle royal, promising to reclaim the federation he says he made his own.

tenures.source: Reappeared unmasked at the close of the Stable Wars broadcast, delivering a cryptic promise to reclaim the promotion he says he first won a battle royal for in April 1998 before vanishing four months later.

name: Brody Stevens
caption: The promotion's own ring announcer across every card in this record.

tenures.source: Billed as the ring announcer on every card in this record.

name: Joey Piles
caption: One half of the promotion's own broadcast team until the owner fired him on camera midway through the promotion's own "Sh*t Happens" broadcast.

tenures.source: Called play-by-play across the promotion's first broadcasts before being fired on air by the promotion's own owner and replaced by Clint Cornell.

name: Ryan Reynolds
caption: The promotion's own color commentator across every card in this record.

tenures.source: Called color commentary on every card in this record, continuing after his broadcast partner was fired on air.

name: Clint Cornell
caption: A backstage interviewer promoted to the broadcast booth after the promotion's own owner fired his broadcast partner on camera.

tenures.source: Conducted a backstage interview with the promotion's own Commissioner on 9 February; hired into the broadcast booth by the promotion's own owner on 15 February after Joey Piles was fired.

name: Billy Gilmour
caption: A recurring referee across the promotion's own broadcasts.

tenures.source: Refereed the Ironman Championship matches on 24 January and 9 February, among other bouts.

name: Joe Gainer
caption: A referee who worked the promotion's own debut match between Maxx Carnage and Chris Douvalas.

tenures.source: Refereed the Maxx Carnage vs. Chris Douvalas debut match on 9 February.

name: Dan Falk
caption: The promotion's own on-screen Owner and President, who fired one half of his own broadcast team live on the air.

tenures.source: Billed throughout as the promotion's own Owner and President; added a stipulation to the Ironman Championship match on 9 February and fired commentator Joey Piles on air on 15 February.

name: "The Swirlie King" Marvin
caption: One half of the tag team the Disfunctional Duo, whose running gag is a toaster he calls Toasty.

tenures.source: Lost as the Disfunctional Duo on 9 February to War Ensemble; won as the Disfunctional Duo on 15 February over the Mighty Mighty Posers.

name: "Dillusional" Dominic Hextall
caption: The other half of the Disfunctional Duo, who won the tag team's first match of the record with his own toaster as an impromptu weapon.

tenures.source: Lost as the Disfunctional Duo on 9 February to War Ensemble; won as the Disfunctional Duo on 15 February over the Mighty Mighty Posers.

name: "The Corporate Whore" Chris Kisass
caption: One half of the tag team the Mighty Mighty Posers, who lost to the Disfunctional Duo.

tenures.source: Lost as the Mighty Mighty Posers to the Disfunctional Duo on 15 February.

name: "Trendy" Travis Montgomery
caption: The other half of the Mighty Mighty Posers, who lost to the Disfunctional Duo despite a roll of quarters concealed in his tights.

tenures.source: Lost as the Mighty Mighty Posers to the Disfunctional Duo on 15 February, having briefly used a roll of quarters as a weapon.

name: Tony Tellez
caption: A henchman aligned with Tony T's stable who interfered in the promotion's own Internet Championship gimmick match.

tenures.source: Interfered in the Internet Championship gimmick match on 24 January, briefly turning the tide against the champion before the challenger recovered.
